scope: Separate nominal CAD family, M4 to M24, 12 coarse and 14 fine combinations; no CSN equivalence claim

corrections.source: Aspen PDF page 2, maximum hexagon height m, M10
corrections.evidence: Böllhoff M10 m max 8.0 mm and original DIN 1587:1987 table m max 8 mm; 88 mm would also exceed the 18 mm overall height

model_choices.across_flats: Nominal ISO wrench widths; do not substitute legacy Bossard stock widths for M10/M12/M14/M22
model_choices.crown: Cylindrical stem plus hemispherical crown at the tabulated approximate radius
model_choices.bore_depth: Selected CAD depth min(h - w_min, t + pitch). Keep the tabulated minimum pole wall while avoiding an unnecessarily deep bore; separate from usable thread depth t.
model_choices.thread_depth: Midpoint of tabulated t minimum/maximum interval
model_choices.internal_geometry: Flat-bottom nominal bore with finite schematic thread/run-out. This is not a manufactured thread or detailed DIN 76-1 tooling/undercut model.
model_choices.material: Generic steel, density 7850 kg/m3; no unsupported strength-class or coating certification

edition_limits: The 2021 preview confirms scope and freedom to select run-out or undercut, but omits the detailed dimension pages. Do not claim a complete 2021 manufacturing validation from that preview. The original 1987 scan establishes the pole-wall and separate t construction; use the manufacturer nominal dimensions for this CAD family.
